name: Glitch GIF
summary: A looped clip with torn bands, split colour channels and repeated frames, as if the signal failed. Artists on Tumblr and in net art circles made it common after 2010.

philosophy.core_thesis: A fault in the signal is an image: show the error, do not hide it.
design_principles: Shift the red channel by 3px to the left and the blue channel by 3px to the right on each glitch frame.
Cut 3 to 8 horizontal bands of 4px to 40px height and move each sideways by 10px to 60px.
Run the glitch in bursts of 2 to 6 frames inside a loop of 20 to 40 frames at 12 fps.
Keep 60% of the frames clean, so that the error reads as an error.
Limit the palette to 64 colours and keep the dither visible.
Set text as a mono line at 14px with 2 duplicate offsets in red and cyan at 40% opacity.
Place a scanline layer of 2px stripes at 8% opacity over the frame.
anti_patterns: A fully corrupted loop with no clean frame
Smooth gradients with no channel split
Slow dissolves in place of hard cuts
Photographic noise with no band structure

layout.grid_mechanics: A free stack of frames and text lines on a 12-column grid with 8px gutters; bands break the grid by 10px to 60px.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 15% to 25% of the surface stays empty; the spacing scale is 4, 8, 16 and 32px.
layout.alignment_rules: The main frame sits centred; text lines sit flush-left with offset duplicates of 3px.
layout.container_geometry: Rectangular frames with a 0px radius and a 2px cyan edge; a hard offset shadow in red and cyan.

font_pairings.note: An open display face with cut bands, with a mono text face.
A terminal face for a quieter glitch page.

hierarchy_rules: Set 1 display line at 48px or more and keep body text at 16px with no effect.
Duplicate a display line twice, in red and cyan, with offsets of 3px.

color.palette_structure: Near-black ground with a red and a cyan channel colour in equal weight, and white text.
color.contrast_rules: Signal white on dead signal holds 17:1; red and cyan carry offsets and edges, not body text.
color.surface_treatment: Flat dark panels; a scanline overlay at 8% opacity and a band tear on hover.
color.light_and_shadow: A hard offset shadow of 3px in red on the right and cyan on the left; no soft shadow.

materiality.surface_simulation: A failing video signal: CRT scan lines, channel drift and compression blocks.
materiality.border_rules: A 2px cyan line; on hover the line splits into red and cyan with 3px offset.
materiality.blur_and_elevation: No blur; the offset shadow is hard.

ornamentation_details.iconography: Solid pixel glyphs at 24px with square terminals.
ornamentation_details.illustration: Portraits, statues and city scenes with channel split and torn bands.

motion.transition_physics: Clean frames run for 0.5s to 2s, then a burst of 2 to 6 glitch frames at 12 fps; no easing inside a burst.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover starts a 3-frame band tear; active inverts the red and cyan channels for 1 frame.

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels unease and fascination at a machine that breaks.

use_cases: title cards for dark, edgy content
avoid_when: The audience has photosensitive epilepsy risk and the loop flashes more than 3 times in 1 second.
The page needs a calm tone.

modifiers.how: Remove the bursts and let one small part of the frame move in a slow loop.
Replace the neon pair with silver and baby blue and add chrome type.
Cut the palette to 16 colours and snap every band to an 8px grid.

pack.why: Hard pixel glyphs match the block noise and the square terminals of a broken signal.

ground.why: A glitch loop shows the scan lines of the failing video signal.

sources.title: Rosa Menkman, The Glitch Moment(um) (Institute of Network Cultures, 2011)
